newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy party leaders begin welfare meeting.
newsitem.headline: Italy party leaders begin welfare meeting.

text.p: Leaders of parties supporting Italy's centre-left coalition government began a meeting on Monday to discuss plans to reform the welfare state.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi opened talks last week with Italy's three main union confederations, trade bodies and employers' group Confindustria on the thorny question of reforms of the welfare state and Italy's generous pensions system.
But Sergio Cofferati, head of the CGIL union, said last week that the position was inadequate and that a strike might be inevitable if the government did not adopt common positions.
Hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti, whose party provides the coalition with its majority in the lower house of parliament, has said the government document was a "false start".

Italy is under pressure to carry out a convincing reform of social spending -- and to shake up its pensions system -- to prove that public finances will be kept under control before the planned 1999 launch of the single European currency.

The Prodi document called for a review of a generous early retirement system which allows Italians to draw a pension based on the length of service rather than because they have reached retirement age, questioning whether the country could afford it.
Bertinotti was attending Monday's meeting, as was Massimo D'Alema, head of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), largest party in Prodi's coalition, and parliamentary group leaders.
